title: LaTCoder: Converting Webpage Design to Code with Layout-as-Thought

problem.claim: Design-to-code systems must convert webpage designs into functional front-end code while preserving the visual layout.

gap.claim: Recent multimodal large language models often fail to accurately preserve webpage layout during code generation.

contributions.claim: LaTCoder uses Layout-as-Thought to enhance layout preservation during webpage design-to-code generation.
The approach divides webpage designs into image blocks using a simple algorithm.
The approach generates code for each block with a Chain-of-Thought-based prompt, assembles outputs using absolute positioning or an MLLM-based method, and dynamically selects the output.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present LaTCoder, a novel approach based on Layout-as-Thought for improving layout preservation in webpage design code generation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: LaTCoder was evaluated with DeepSeek-VL2, Gemini, and GPT-4o on a public benchmark and the newly introduced CC-HARD benchmark featuring complex layouts.
The authors report significant improvements on automatic metrics.
With DeepSeek-VL2, TreeBLEU increased by 66.67% and MAE decreased by 38% compared with direct prompting.

narrative_sequence.summary: Design-to-code connects visual webpage design with functional implementation for front-end development.
Existing multimodal large language models can fail to preserve webpage layout during code generation.
LaTCoder applies Layout-as-Thought through block decomposition, block-level code generation, alternative assembly strategies, and dynamic selection.
The method is evaluated across multiple backbone models and both public and complex-layout benchmarks.
The authors report improved automatic metrics and favorable human preferences, including a TreeBLEU increase of 66.67%, an MAE decrease of 38%, and preference in over 60% of cases.

source_observation.claim: The method decomposes a webpage design into image blocks before generating code.

interpretation.claim: Breaking a complex visual structure into localized regions may help a generative model preserve layout details.

application.claim: For visual-to-code generation, consider region-level decomposition before localized generation.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether block decomposition helps across all webpage structures or model families.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the benchmark sizes, datasets, or evaluation protocols.
The abstract does not report results for each backbone model and benchmark separately.
The abstract does not provide implementation details for the assembly strategies or dynamic selection.
